explanations.answer: They all go in search of him
explanations.explanation: That's exactly it, friend. The text says the Philistines "…all went in search of him…" (2 Samuel 5:17). Not a few of them, ALL of them. They heard David had been anointed king over Israel, and the whole crowd came looking.

explanations.answer: They pull back to their own land
explanations.explanation: Not this one, friend. Pulling back isn't what the text says. When the Philistines heard David had been anointed king over Israel, they "…all went in search of him…" (2 Samuel 5:17). Backing off would be the quiet option, and this crowd wasn't feeling quiet.

explanations.answer: They wait to see what he does
explanations.explanation: Good guess, friend, but the text doesn't say they waited. When they heard David had been anointed king over Israel, they "…all went in search of him…" (2 Samuel 5:17). That's a crowd with their shoes already on.

Yes, friend. David learned of the search, and the text says he "…went down to the stronghold." (2 Samuel 5:17). A stronghold is a fortified place built to hold up against attack. Smart spot to be when a whole nation is looking for you.
Close, friend, but it's not the palace. The verse says David "…went down to the stronghold." (2 Samuel 5:17). A stronghold is a fortified place, built for trouble. A palace is for comfy chairs.
Not the temple, friend. The text says David "…went down to the stronghold." (2 Samuel 5:17). That's a fortified place, a spot made to hold up when enemies come looking.

explanations.answer: He asks the LORD what to do
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. The Philistines were spread out in the Valley of Rephaim, and "…David inquired of the LORD…" (2 Samuel 5:19). When the question was whether to go up against them, he took it straight to God. I know plenty of folks who ask LAST.

Reasonable thing to do, friend, but the text doesn't say he did it. It says "…David inquired of the LORD…" (2 Samuel 5:19). He asked God whether he should go up against the Philistines, not how many men he had.

explanations.answer: He sends out a few spies
explanations.explanation: Spies would make a good movie, friend, but they're not in this passage. What the text says is "…David inquired of the LORD…" (2 Samuel 5:19). He went straight to God with his question.

Not quite, friend, and this one's False. The LORD didn't say stay put. He said, "Go up," and added, "for I will surely deliver the Philistines into your hand." (2 Samuel 5:19). Waiting for them to leave on their own was never the plan.

Right, friend. Nothing about staying in the stronghold. The LORD answered, "Go up," and said, "for I will surely deliver the Philistines into your hand." (2 Samuel 5:19). He told David to go AND gave him a promise to go with it.

Yes, friend. David says, "Like a bursting flood, the LORD has burst out against my enemies before me." (2 Samuel 5:20). He gives the credit to the LORD, not to himself. Then he named the place Baal-perazim.
Close, friend, but David didn't credit the army. He said, "Like a bursting flood, the LORD has burst out against my enemies before me." (2 Samuel 5:20). The one bursting out was the LORD.
Easy one to guess, since David was the new king. But he said, "Like a bursting flood, the LORD has burst out against my enemies before me." (2 Samuel 5:20). He pointed to the LORD, not to himself.
Not this time, friend, it's False. The text says the Philistines abandoned their idols there, "…and David and his men carried them away." (2 Samuel 5:21). Nobody left them lying in the dirt.

That's right, friend. The Philistines abandoned their idols, and the text says "…David and his men carried them away." (2 Samuel 5:21). Those idols did not stay put. Left behind by their own people, and then hauled off like a pile of junk.
Not so, friend, it's False. David didn't skip a step. The text says "…David inquired of the LORD…" again (2 Samuel 5:23). The earlier win didn't replace the new question.

Right on, friend. The same enemy came back to the same valley, but "…David inquired of the LORD…" again (2 Samuel 5:23). He didn't coast on the last win. I once stamped the same shape the same way for years, so I know how tempting a routine is.
That's it, friend. The LORD said, "Do not march straight up, but circle around behind them and attack them in front of the balsam trees." (2 Samuel 5:23). Same enemy, but a new plan.
That's the exact thing the LORD said NOT to do, friend. His words were, "Do not march straight up, but circle around behind them…" (2 Samuel 5:23). So no straight charge this time.

Not quite, friend. The LORD gave David a plan with action in it: "…circle around behind them and attack them in front of the balsam trees." (2 Samuel 5:23). There's a sound to listen for in the treetops, and then the word is "move quickly" (2 Samuel 5:24). Nothing about waiting for the Philistines to leave.

explanations.answer: The sound of marching in the treetops
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The LORD said, "As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move quickly…" (2 Samuel 5:24). Think about that. The signal wasn't a horn or a flag. It was a sound up in the branches.

explanations.answer: A trumpet blast from the hills
explanations.explanation: A trumpet would be a nice clear signal, friend, but it's not what the LORD said. The signal was "…the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees…" (2 Samuel 5:24). David had to listen up in the branches.

explanations.answer: A loud shout from the camp
explanations.explanation: Good guess, friend, but a shout isn't in the text. The LORD said, "As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move quickly…" (2 Samuel 5:24). The sound came from the treetops.

explanations.answer: The LORD has gone out before him
explanations.explanation: That's right, friend. The LORD said the sound "…will mean that the LORD has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines." (2 Samuel 5:24). The sound was not just a cue to go. It told David the LORD was already out ahead of him.

explanations.answer: The Philistines are ready to retreat
explanations.explanation: Not what the LORD said, friend. He said the sound "…will mean that the LORD has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines." (2 Samuel 5:24). The sound pointed to the LORD going ahead, not to the Philistines packing up.

explanations.answer: His own men are all in place
explanations.explanation: Sensible thought, friend, but that's not what the sound meant. The LORD said it "…will mean that the LORD has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines." (2 Samuel 5:24). It was about where the LORD was, not where the men were.

Yes, friend. The text says, "So David did as the LORD had commanded him…" (2 Samuel 5:25). No tweaking and no shortcuts. That's following the recipe exactly, and my own stamping would have blurred half of it.
Not False, friend. It's True. The text says, "So David did as the LORD had commanded him…" (2 Samuel 5:25). He followed the plan he was given, and he struck down the Philistines from Gibeon to Gezer.
